content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am planning to use [product_name] to manage relays via Modbus-TCP and I want to include a failsafe mechanism. Currently, the controller transmits either an on or off command every five seconds, regardless of state changes. However, my goal is for the relay connected to [product_name] to automatically turn off if, for example, an ON command hasn’t been received within 10 or 15 seconds. At present, my approach is to set a Modbus coil and use that to operate the relay, but this lacks a failsafe function. What would be the best way to implement this? Kind regards, [user_name]
Hello, [product_name] does not include built-in failsafe protocol support. If you use MODBUS TCP, it should work, but failsafe functionality will have to be developed separately.
As a quick suggestion, consider trying a Modbus scan tool.
Hello [user_name], For this setup, you will need to ensure that the relay statuses are accessible through Modbus-TCP. Regards, [user_name] (Translated with Google)

One approach is to send 'heartbeat' signals via Modbus by toggling an unused coil state every five seconds (coil ON, wait, coil OFF, wait, repeat). On the [product_name], link this heartbeat coil network input to a memory flag for monitoring and diagnostics. Then, configure a watchdog mechanism in [product_name] so that if heartbeat signals are absent for more than 20 seconds (the memory flag remains unchanged), the relay automatically switches OFF.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are looking for a dependable failsafe mechanism for relay control over MODBUS-TCP using [product_name]. Built-in failsafe features are absent, so users have developed custom heartbeat monitoring solutions to ensure relays shut off automatically when communication lapses. These manual methods offer a workaround but add complexity and may have reliability limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are hoping for [product_name] to provide an integrated or straightforward way to implement failsafe functionality with MODBUS relay controls, enabling relays to reliably switch off when communication fails.
